name: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest private life insurer by value of new business (VNB): savings (non-par, par, ULIP), protection, annuity/pension and group business sold ~half through banks (HDFC Bank is the largest partner and 50.3% shareholder), plus agency, brokers and direct. H1 FY27 profit Rs1,119cr (+13%), VNB +12% (Moneycontrol, 2026-10-15). Stock Rs543, -27% in 12 months, P/B ~6x, P/E 57 on reported PAT (Rs2,048cr TTM); dependent on distribution economics now under IRDAI review.

exposures.mechanism: IRDAI exposure draft (2026-09-23/24) proposes product-wise commission caps (payout capped at 25%) and a dark-pattern ban. Stock fell ~7% on the day; sector fell up to 26% (PB Fintech). Mechanism: bank/agent distributors earn less -> push less (volumes -5 to -10% in affected savings products) while insurers retain the saved commission (margin +). Net: volumes -5 to -10% in capped products x ~60% of VNB from them => VNB -3 to -6% before cost retention; capitalised at 6x book/long-duration value (value moves more than VNB) => value -7 central (range -14 to +3 if diluted). Systematix says IRDAI 'may need to revisit proposed cap' (BT 2026-09-25) so final rule may be diluted: wide range.

evidence.note: IRDAI proposes lower life insurance commissions, capping payout at 25%; HDFC Life/ICICI Pru Life fell ~7% on the day (Moneycontrol/ET)

exposures.mechanism: +25bp: positive for new-business pricing (guaranteed non-par yields +10-15bp, VNB margin +25-40bp on ~25% margin = +1.5%) and reinvestment; negative for MTM on debt held in non-par/shareholder funds and for discount rate on a 6x book stock (-1). Net +0.5, low confidence; sector has de-rated in rising-yield spells (model observation).

exposures.mechanism: +25bp repo (hiked to 5.50%) -> bank FD rates +20-30bp -> competing savings product becomes more attractive vs non-par savings (not protection/ULIP): savings products ~55% of APE; -2% volume x 55% x margin leverage => -1; partially offset by higher guaranteed rates => -0.6.
